questions.q: He said, “Priyanka (a)/is the most unique (b) /singer of (c)/our college. (d)”
The author is not well known. Little bit people have heard of him.
questions.s:
(d) Few people

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

Mr. Sharma is kind as his father.
questions.s:
The construct 'is....as' is incorrect. We use as + adjective/adverb + as to make comparisons when the things we are comparing are equal in some way. For example:

The world's biggest bull is as big as a small elephant.

Therefore, the phrase in option (c) is the correct choice.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q: He likes to put all the garbage into a black small bag .
questions.s:
Adjectives follow a fixed order :
Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Material → Purpose → Noun
Size comes before colour, so it should be: a small black bag

questions.q: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
questions.s:
The correct option that rectifies the error in the underlined part is colder.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The house seemed much far than she expected.

[MTS 2024]
questions.s:
The correct answer is: "farther"


The sentence compares two distances: the actual distance of the house and what she expected.


For comparisons, the correct form of "far" is "farther" (when referring to physical distance).

questions.q: The Hindu is (1)/ most popular, than any other (2)/ newspaper in India.(3)/ No Error (4)
o: most popular, than any other
questions.s:
When comparing one thing with all others, we must use the superlative degree with a definite article. Also, comparison takes than, but superlative sentences normally use “the most… of/in”.
Correct Sentence: The Hindu is the most popular newspaper in India.

questions.q:

questions.s: When comparing one person to the entire group, the superlative form of "better" is used, which is "best."

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The project was completed / more quicker / than expected.
questions.s: This is an error of double comparison. "Quicker" is already a comparative form of "quick," so adding "more" creates redundancy. It should be either "more quickly" or simply "quicker." Since "quicker" already indicates comparison, "more" is unnecessary and incorrect.

questions.q: Though we both are of the same height (1)/ you are more heavier (2)/ than I. (3)/ No error (4)
o: Though we both are of the same height
you are more heavier
questions.s:
Heavier” is already a comparative degree, so using more + heavier is incorrect because it creates a double comparative.
Correct Sentence: Though we both are of the same height, you are heavier than I.

questions.q: We are witnessing the worse level of income inequality in decades.
o: the worse level of income
questions.s: Replace “worse” with “worst” because the sentence needs the superlative degree.

questions.q: The project is so complex as, if not more complex than, we anticipated.
o: if not more complex than
The project is so complex as,
questions.s:
The correct option is (d) "The project is so complex as."

In English, when comparing degrees of complexity, "as...as" is used with positive degree adjectives and "than" with comparative degree adjectives. Therefore, "so complex as" should be replaced with "as complex as"

The corrected sentence should be: "The project is as complex as, if not more complex than, we anticipated."
